subject: Incremental commit & expansion pricing for new product workloads
messages:
From: Samir Kapoor <samir@leadedgemedia.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: emma@leadedgemedia.com
Date: 2026-11-29T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Pricing for adding a new product line / how commits apply

Hi Aditya —

We’ve been running the Redwood hosted API for our core personalization product and are looking to onboard two additional product teams (recommendation batch scoring + short-form creative generation). Before we schedule an exec call, can you confirm: 

- Whether committed tokens can be shared across multiple products/teams under the same account or if they need separate commits per product.
- How incremental commits are priced (if we add 50M tokens/month on top of our current commit, is there a predictable discount schedule?).
- Any promotional pricing for the first quarter of a cross-product expansion?

Attached a high-level forecast (LE_forecast_q4.csv) — it’s rough but shows expected token mix (70% embeddings, 30% text gen) and a Q1 ramp profile.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 30-min sync if that’s easier.

Samir
VP Product, LeadEdge Media
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir@leadedgemedia.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing for adding a new product line / how commits apply

Samir —

Thanks for the forecast, that helps a lot. Short answers first:

- Shared commits: Yes — for the hosted API we can put multiple products/teams under a single account-level commit. That gives you flexibility to move tokens where you need them.
- Incremental commit pricing: We recommend a tiered approach (see example below). Discounts improve at stable monthly thresholds (e.g., 0-25M @ list, 25-100M @ 8% off, 100-300M @ 14% off, 300M+ @ 20% off). We can make a binding schedule for the committed volume in your SOW.
- Promotional: We can extend a one-time promotional uplift for new workloads — typically a 10–15% introductory credit for the first quarter on incremental volume. I need approval for >12% on the promo.

I attached a starter worksheet (LeadEdge_Q4_commit_proposal.xlsx) with three scenarios: conservative, expected, and aggressive. It shows monthly committed tokens, expected overage, and effective blended per-token price.

Questions for you so we can make the proposal concrete:
- Do you want a single annual commit that spans teams, or quarterly commits that you can reconcile?
- Is predictable latency (SLA) for the generation workloads required (we can model Dedicated capacity if so)?

If it helps, I can draft a phased approach: Month 1–3: add 50M incremental commit at a 12% promo; Month 4–6: move to target committed band with step-up discounts.

Available this afternoon for a quick call.

—Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Kapoor <samir@leadedgemedia.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: emma@leadedgemedia.com
Date: 2026-11-30T08:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing for adding a new product line / how commits apply

Aditya —

Thanks, that structure looks reasonable. A couple of clarifications: 

1) Sharing model: great to know commits can be account-level. Are there any guardrails (e.g., per-team quotas) we should expect to set on your side? We want to avoid one team soaking the tokens.
2) Rollover / unused tokens: do monthly unused committed tokens roll over? If not, can we get a carry-forward credit for an annual commit?
3) Overage: what is the typical overage multiplier (list price * x)?

I attached a slightly expanded forecast (LE_forecast_q4.csv) with per-team token splits. We expect an initial ramp: 0 -> 30M tokens for product B over two months and then steady state ~75M by month 6.

If you can sketch the phased commit with concrete dollar examples (we’re aiming for a CFO-friendly one-page), that’ll help.

Samir
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir@leadedgemedia.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing for adding a new product line / how commits apply

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 10:12 AM, aditya_rao wrote:
> Aditya —
>
> Thanks for the forecast, that helps a lot. Short answers first:

Samir — pulling in some concrete numbers from pricing ops and a recommended path to keep the finance team happy. High level proposal (monthly figures):

- Phase A (Months 1–3): Add incremental 50M tokens/month as a temporary add-on. Pricing: incremental tokens priced at list less 12% promo credit for Q1.
- Phase B (Months 4–6): Convert to recurring commit: 150M/month committed. New blended discount schedule applied (25–100M @8%, 100–300M @14%). Effective blended discount in example = ~13.2%.
- Rollover / carry-forward: For hosted, we do not auto-rollover month-to-month. For annual prepay commits, we offer a limited carry-forward credit policy (up to 10% of annual commit, applied in final quarter).
- Overage: Overages billed at list price * 1.15 (i.e., 15% premium above list) unless you convert overage into an add-on commit within 14 days.

Example one-pager (pulled into the attached LeadEdge_Q4_commit_proposal.xlsx): shows sample invoice math and effective $/k-token under each scenario.

Approvals needed: I can approve up to 12% promo for Q1. For 13%+, we need credit approval (cc’ing Karthik). If you want 12% now and a retro bonus if you hit the aggressive target in month 3, we can do that.

Next steps: 1) Confirm you want a single account-level commit that spans teams; 2) pick Phase A size (50M vs 75M); 3) schedule a 30-min pricing review so I can finalize the SOW and DocuSign.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Kapoor <samir@leadedgemedia.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:06:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing for adding a new product line / how commits apply

Marissa / Aditya —

Quick follow-ups: 
- Understood re: no automatic monthly rollovers for hosted. For the annual-carry-forward credit, can you confirm that the 10% cap applies to product-level usage or account-level? We’d prefer account-level so teams can reallocate.
- SLA / latency credits: We will need latency SLOs for the creative gen workload. If the hosted tier can’t guarantee that, we’ll need pricing for Dedicated (estimate: required p95 < 300ms for gen).
- Contractual clause: any chance for a 30-day review clause for the first quarter to adjust committed volume without penalty? CFO wants a safety valve during ramp.

If you can update the one-pager with the answers above we’ll be ready to run to legal.

Samir
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir@leadedgemedia.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T14:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing for adding a new product line / how commits apply

Samir —

Thanks — answers below and I attached the revised pricing workbook (pricing-model-v3.csv) with the updated examples.

- Carry-forward credit: applies at the account level (so you can reallocate across teams). The 10% cap is on aggregate annual committed volume, not per-product.
- SLA / latency: hosted tier maintains best-effort latency; for guaranteed p95 < 300ms we recommend Dedicated. I included a Dedicated cost estimate in the workbook and a simple breakeven for when Dedicated makes sense (roughly at sustained >150M gen tokens/month with tight latency SLOs).
- 30-day review clause: we can include a one-time 30-day review window in the SOW for the first quarter that allows a +/-25% adjustment to the incremental commit without penalty; any changes beyond that will be addressed via standard amendment. This needs legal sign-off but we’ve done this for other customers.

Next steps:
1) If you’re good with account-level commit + Phase A = 50M/month, I’ll route the SOW for a 12% promo and include the 30-day review clause.
2) Marissa will prepare the DocuSign (Hub record: https://hub.redwood.ai/deals/D-2026-1107-LEADEDGE).
3) We’ll hold a short call with engineering if you want to validate latency expectations before signing.

If you confirm, I’ll send DocuSign tonight.

—Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing-model-v3.csv
